utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Unless there's anything that I'm not aware of, we can call the next witness, Mr. Dragan Jasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, if you could please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could please sit down. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasovic. Can you understand me all right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. If at any time you don't understand one of my questions, please just tell me and I'll try to rephrase it in a more clear way. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, in a moment I'll ask you some questions about your personal and professional background, but before I do that I would just like to ask you a couple of brief questions about your prior interviews and meetings with the Prosecution. First, did you give a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 12 May 2004?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review that statement and make any corrections that were necessary?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you make those corrections this weekend?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, did you meet with me in Belgrade earlier this year on 21st of February, 2005?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And do you remember if you've met on any other occasions with a Prosecution investigator in Belgrade this year or last year besides the two that I've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I do. This year I met with Mr. Roel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, but I met with him two or three times, around a month ago. Maybe more than a month ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. And finally, you and I met over the weekend and then on Monday to prepare for your testimony. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, now I'll ask you some questions about your personal and professional background. First, is your full name Dragan Jasovic and your father's name Nikola?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were you born on 20th September 1953 in Pec, Kosova?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And you are of Serb ethnicity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, what languages do you speak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I speak Serbian and the Siptari Albanian language. I speak a little Russian, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is it correct that you completed secondary school in 1973?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And after secondary school you completed your national service with the Yugoslav army in 1974. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I served in Podgorica which is in the Republic of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Currently I am a crime investigation policeman, a regular inspector in the secretariat of the interior in the town of Urosevac but I am working in a town in Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, how long have you been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I started as a policeman on the 1st of July, 1975, in Stimlje. Municipality in Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What were your duties at that time in Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I worked as a policeman and later as a leader of the security sector. I worked on the beat, in patrol duty, covering areas that the police station of Stimlje had as their area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you receive any training as a police officer at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, before I started working I completed training in Djakovica in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, how long did you work as a police officer in Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: From the 1st of May, 1975, until the 1st of May, 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you change jobs on the 1st of May in 1981?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My superior in the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac appointed me assistant commander of the police station in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What were your duties as assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I would not like to expand on my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Well, it can be brief, but just tell me what kind of work you were doing as assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: As assistant commander of the police station I was in charge of the policemen who worked on the beat and on patrol duty. It mainly boiled down to preventive police work, that is preventing crimes and working to detect the perpetrators of crimes where perpetrators were unknown as well as general law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you based as of 1981?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: In Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In the headquarters in the Urosevac SUP? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the base of the secretariat of the interior, because the SUP of Urosevac covered Stimlje, Strpce and Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned Stimlje, Strpce, and Kacanik. Are those is in addition to Urosevac municipality itself? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Actually Kacanik was a separate municipality whereas Stimlje and Strpce were included in our municipality. I cannot remember in which year. It could have been 1989 or maybe earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. But they were all included under the responsibility of the SUP of Urosevac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The SUP of Urosevac was the headquarters, the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did your duties change in any way in 1986?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: In 1986 in the area of Urosevac, mainly in the village of Gornje Nerodimlje and other places, we had a number of incidents of physical assault; various offences committed in the fields; interception of Serbian children; damaged incurred to orchards and crops. Whereas the victims were mainly people of Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did this have an effect on the duties you personally undertook at that time? What kind of work were you doing as of 1986?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the orders of our superiors in the SUP of Urosevac - at the time the superior was Mr. Stankovic, nicknamed Lacko - I was transferred to be an assistant to my Albanian colleague. I don't remember -- in fact, I would not like to mention his name in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go briefly into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, please don't mention the name but how would you describe your working relationship with your partner?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: My working relationship with him. I have to say at the time that that period I told you about was characterised by the great number of crimes where perpetrators were unknown. We patrolled the area of Urosevac, Stimlje, and Kacanik together, trying to prevent interethnic conflicts. We performed all our duties and assignments together and we had mutual respect for each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How long did you work together with this partner?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: From 1986 until I believe the beginning of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And again, without mentioning his name, can you just briefly explain why you stopped working with him or why you are no longer working with him after 1990?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I stopped working with him because he had problems caused to him by his fellow Albanians but also by inspectors in the SUP of Urosevac who told him that he was a traitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: After that, after 1990, did you continue to work on the same kinds of cases as you had worked on with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I did continue, but my Albanian colleague transferred to other duties in the secretariat of the interior of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that. At this point did you work alone or did you get new partners that you worked with, new colleagues?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I worked on my job alone, but my direct superior gave me two Albanian assistants, also members of the SUP of Urosevac, who by that time had still remained in the SUP of our town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This may have been later in time, but who is Momcilo Sparavalo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Momcilo Sparavalo is a colleague who joined me in end 1996, or maybe 1997. He is also an inspector at the secretariat of the interior of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, now I'm going to move away from questions about your background. There's some questions about the procedures that you used to investigate cases, in particular in the year 1998. My first question is this: Generally speaking, what kinds of crimes did you investigate in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: 1998, Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo and I worked on jobs involving crimes of terrorism, genocide and the crime which is called "crime of association with the purpose of committing hostile activities and terrorist activities."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I want to ask you how a particular investigation would begin. What would trigger an investigation for you to look into a particular incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: You mean in a specific incident? When something happened, it could be reported by members of the family, immediate family, or extended family, or by any citizen in the street. I'm now talking about the municipality of Stimlje. Sometimes we received reports from the police station in Stimlje, from policemen or commanders who worked in Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever obtain information from paid informants? Just speaking generally now. You don't have to mention any names.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I had one registered informant, one source.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session for a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, in fact I'll return to that line of questioning in a moment. I'm going to move on to something different. During your investigations, did you conduct interviews?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Where did -- where would those interviews take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: All interviews would be conducted on the premises of the secretariat of the interior of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that if you were meeting with a friendly source, you would meet somewhere outside of the SUP premises. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Outside the premises and mainly in late evening hours or the small hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you have the ability to summons people in for questioning or even arrest people for questioning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: My colleague Sparavalo and I never left our offices. If any people were taken into custody, they would be taken into custody by regular policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay, I understand that. My question is a little different. Maybe not you personally detaining people, but if you wanted to talk to someone, could you send police officers out to bring that person in for questioning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: My method of work never involved sending policemen to bring somebody for questioning. I would usually arrange it through friends, all of them people of ethnic -- sorry, Albanian ethnicity and mainly by telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were people ever brought in for interviews involuntarily, people that didn't voluntarily show up asking to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now I'm going to turn to the process of taking statements. Can you describe the process by which you would take a signed statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the taking of statements is concerned, it all depended, as I told you before. If somebody from the immediate family or any citizen in the street came to us to report an incident, they would first come into contact with the duty service, the duty policeman; and the duty policeman would inform me that somebody came to report an incident. I had my own method of work. I would talk to that person and I would make notes in my notepad. I would make a draft. In order to establish that the person was giving me correct information, I would come back several times during the same day to the initial point of the interview because if the person was telling the truth all the data would be the same every time, all the information he gave me would be the same every time he told the story again; and if not, then that would be also established in the process. After this draft was made, then the person would sign the statement and my colleague and I would affix our signatures as well. In addition to the statement we would also file a criminal report if we estimated that elements of a criminal offence were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you a couple of follow-up questions on what you told us. Focusing on the mechanism of how a statement was typed up, how did that work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the typing itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's right. Did you type it? Did someone else type it? Who typed it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The typing was done by my colleague, Momcilo Sparavalo, while I dictated. Since I know the Albanian language rather well, every statement would be interpreted to the person on the spot, and I must say that all Albanians mainly knew the Serbian language. I mean the people who came to report crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And just to be clear, did the person making the statement then have some opportunity to review the statement or make some corrections before they signed it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I would dictate the statement aloud to my colleague, Momcilo Sparavalo, after which I would give the statement to the person who came to report the incident to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And would this happen on one day or over the course of several days? How long did this usually take, this process?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: A statement would usually be completed within a day; however, there was some cases when the party who came to report the crime knew the last name of the perpetrator or knew only the first name. In that case, I would tell them to come back in a day or two when they found out the name. That was my way of working.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And now I want to focus on the content of a statement. What information was included in the signed statement? And I guess -- perhaps I can ask a more clear question. Did you include your own comments or any other extraneous information in the signed statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to a statement made by someone reporting an incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement would contain everything the person had said, I mean everything the person said was included. Nothing was included that came from myself or my colleague, Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sir, did you sometimes make official notes instead of statements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Official notes and information was something I wrote up in those cases where no statement was taken. For the most part, these notes and this information which I wrote contained information obtained from persons of Albanian ethnicity. But I did not include the names of the persons who had given us the information. I kept that information in my own notebook for the security of those persons and the security of their immediate and extended families.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When would you draft an official note after you -- after, say, your first meeting where you received information from someone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I drew up all official notes on the premises of where my offices were. I couldn't do that in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I guess my question is: Relative to obtaining the information, when did you write it up? Did you write it up the same day? Every Friday? The last day of every month? When would you do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I had my own method of work. I never compiled information provided only by one source. I always endeavoured -- if I, for example, received the same information from three different persons, then I would draw up a note or information; and there is a difference between a note and an information. And if I was convinced that the source was telling the truth, then I would draw up information based on only one source.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You make a distinction between a note and an information. Can you explain what the difference is, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The difference is the following: Information is when you learn for the first time about something. After that, official notes are drawn up. For example, you learn about a kidnapping; afterwards, the file is updated and official notes are drawn up. I don't know if I've made it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I understand. Yes, thank you. Mr. Jasovic, when you took a statement or made an official note, did you consider it important that those documents be accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was not working for myself. If I wrote something that was untrue, I would be deceiving the secretariat of interior affairs; and in my view, this was a great and important institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you ever force witnesses to give you information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never descended to such mean things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever mistreat witnesses in order to get information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you investigate an incident differently depending on whether or not the victim was a Serb or an Albanian or from some other ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior, the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac, regardless of ethnic origin, religious affiliation, or whatever always treated every case equally because there was no division in the Ministry of the Interior. We did not -- we did not separate people according to whether they were Albanians or Serbs and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You've told us about the Ministry of the Interior, but I'm interested in you personally. Did you personally investigate incidents differently depending on whether or not the victim might have been a Serb or an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I used the same methods both towards Albanians, Serbs, Roma, or any other -- a person of any other ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. We've spent a little bit time talking about your background and procedures. Now I'm going to move to a new topic. And I would mention that if today we look at any documents or we talk about any interviews where you've deviated from these procedures that you've just told us about, please tell me. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you learn about any underground or illegal activity in Petrastica in the early 1990s?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: In the early 1990s, we as a service learned that in that area an illegal organisation entitled Balli Kombetar had been established. We learned that weapons had been transferred from the area of Drenica to the village of Petrastica, municipality of Stimlje. I must mention that until 1989 Petrastica had belonged to Lipjan municipality and from that time to Stimlje municipality. After this the people's movement of Kosova was established and this existed until the KLA staffs were established in early June 1998. This popular movement from the Republic of Kosovo formed its sabotage groups on the 22nd of April, 1996. In the evening in Kosovo and Metohija we had several terrorist actions, one of which was carried out in Stimlje, where on the 26th of April, 1996, a policeman was killed. His name was Milenko Bucic. And on the 28th of November, 1997, in the village of Petrastica an honest Siptar, Dalib Dugovi was killed in front of his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When did you first hear about the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about the KLA for the first time in early 1998, and I'm referring to Stimlje municipality, when the first staff was established in the village of Rance and Isak Musliu, also known as Qerqiz, was appointed commander. In early June, through representatives of the DSK, Ibrahim Rugova's party -- the LDK, he organised a meeting in a mosque. Mr. Isak Musliu was opposed by members of the DSK. The meeting was held in a mosque with three other persons wearing camouflage uniforms with KLA insignia and they were armed with automatic weapons and short barrels. The meeting was led by Isak Musliu, who on that occasion said that a staff had been established in the village of Rance and that the KLA was taking over power, that as of that time there were no more Albanian parties - what shall I call them? - and that everybody had to comply with orders issued by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Let me interrupt you right there for a moment, please. What village did this meeting take place in, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: In the village of Racak in the mosque. The village of Racak is in Stimlje municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And you mentioned Isak Musliu. Did you know Isak Musliu?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him personally. He and Mr. Srboljub Vojinovic -- I'm not sure when, but between 1993 and 1995 sat in a cafe in Stimlje owned by Murat Gashi, as known as Sultan, from the village of Petrastica, municipality of Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You mentioned another person Srboljub and I missed the last name. Who was that person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: An inspector of the state security service in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, before 1998 did you have social contact like this with other people who eventually joined the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I did. Mr. Isak Musliu was the commander of the KLA in the village of Rance, and after that the military police in Rucak Muhali [phoen] in Stimlje municipality, the village of Petrove. I had contacts Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with his KLA deputy in the village of Rance, Zymer Kurtishi, because as a policeman in Stimlje I ate and had tea in the house of Zymer Kurtishi on more than one occasion. I know his father personally. I also knew his grandfather. And he moved from Rance to another village in Stimlje municipality, Uzecani [phoen]. I knew Jete Jashari, also known as Juri, from the village of Grejcevce, Suva Reka municipality. One of the commanders of the KLA in Topilo, Laniste, Devetak, and before that he was in Grejcevce. These were all villages. I knew Ramadan Behluli from the village of Crnoljevo, Stimlje municipality, and with my Albanian colleagues who were also inspectors. In May 1997 I was in his house in the village of Crnoljevo where we had tea.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. On the time you said you sat in a cafe in Stimlje with Isak Musliu, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Just having a drink. Regardless of ethnic origin in Stimlje people had alcoholic drinks. Srboljub Vojinovic knew him and introduced us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, getting back to the meeting in Racak that you discussed a moment ago, you don't need to name names right now, but in general from whom did you receive this information about the meeting in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I received information from more than one source because there were statements made by several Albanians and also from operations connections because at that meeting the civilian protection was established and a body for the procurement of weapons, food, fuel, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Did any of these sources of information say how they knew that it was Isak Musliu who led the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sure. Of course I will. How did these sources know that it was Isak Musliu who led the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This leaked in Racak, from the villagers, because they knew him. Most of the people in the village of Racak were decent people, honest people of Albanian ethnicity who opposed the establishment of the KLA and did not wish to join it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you speak with anyone who was actually present at the meeting? There's no need to give a name, but I just want to know if you spoke with anyone who was present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I probably did, but I can't recall now. There are probably statements available and in the statement they would say whether they had attended the meeting or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll show you some documents in a minute. Before I do, did you ever hear about similar meetings in other villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Similar meeting were held in early July, or rather in June 1998. There was a meeting in the village of Petrastica, Stimlje municipality, chaired by Shukri Buja, later the commander of the 161st Brigade for the area of Urosevac and Ramiz Qeriqi. Shukri Buja was in the village of Sokoli. On the 13th of June there was a meeting in the village of Crnoljevo, Stimlje municipality. And I have to say that in Petrastica the meeting was held in Idriza Ajeti primary school and in Crnoljevo it was held in the courtyard of a cafe, the name of which I don't know. In the village of Zborce the meeting was chaired by Fatmir Limaj, known as Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Just for one point of clarity, on the transcript it reads that Shukri Buja was in the village of Sokoli. What did you say again about Sokoli?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: He had a pseudonym, Gazetar. That was his in nickname. After that they called him Sokoli.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, with the assistance of the usher and Mr. Younis, Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to show you a document. I'm going to hand you a binder full of documents and the usher will help you turn to tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps for the record the B/C/S version of this bears the ERN K00225655 to 5667. And the English is 0304-8619 to 8621. Again, it's behind tab 17. And it is a statement. The attachment page on the front says "Dated 8th September 1998," but I believe the statement itself is dated 17 September 1998. We'll put this on Sanction if that's easier for people to follow along. We have the English version on Sanction with some redactions made to protect the identity of the people who gave the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, have a look at this statement. Your name appears on the last page. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Are you referring to the statement of the 8th of September, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you. And again, we're in public session now, so please do your best not to mention a name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. The statement was taken by me, Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo, Srboljub Vojinovic and Miroslav Antic. Sparavalo and I were from the public security station and the other two were from the state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Does your signature appear on the copy that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know why that might be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Because I kept all statements for myself and the main statements with the signature were delivered to the chief of the secretariat of the interior and our files.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Were you present when this statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: All persons mentioned, all the authorised officials mentioned in the statement were present, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Witness, we're in open session again, so please be careful with names. If you look at the first paragraph of this statement, the statement says -- well, actually, in fact, if you could read that first paragraph to yourself. You don't need to read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: From the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yeah. Not out loud, just read it quietly to yourself there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is reading, just a technical comment. If you push computer evidence on your monitors, it's a lot more clear than if you push video evidence. I don't know which one you're using.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, just briefly, does this refer to the meeting in Racak which you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to the village of Racak where this person stated he had not attended the meeting because he was a member of the presidency of the DSK, the Kosovo Democratic Union, and he did not wish to join the KLA. And the contact of Mr. Isak Musliu with a person whose name I would not like to mention is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did this person say who had chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the person said that the meeting was chaired by Mr. Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could turn to the -- I believe it's the next page at the very top of the page. If we could move to the next page in English also. Is there a reference there to Milaim Kamberi at the top?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the name of Milaim Kamberi, son of Rexhep, from Racak is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What does it say about him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: It says that in July 1998 they forcibly seized him from his house, that is the members of the so-called KLA, and they took him towards Drenica. After that we discovered that Milaim Kamberi had had a property dispute with another Albanian concerning his courtyard and he reported this to the police station in Stimlje. But the Albanian terrorists, the so-called KLA, did not like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm going to move to another document now. If you could look behind tab 12. Perhaps the usher could assist you. The ERN for this document is K032-7273.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It's also showing on Sanction, the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a statement received by me and Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo, my colleague, my partner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could go briefly into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to direct your attention to -- I guess it's the second paragraph and I'll read something and just follow along. It says that: "A meeting had been held in the elementary school in the village of Zborce." And then a little further along it says a person "informed me that the meeting had been chaired by a person named Celiku, who said that Siptar political parties in the village of Godance were no longer valid and that a terrorist group, the so-called OVK, would be taking over. He said that representatives of the so-called OVK would be coming from Zborce." Now, is that information told to you by the person we just mentioned in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the person who gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is this a reference to the meeting in Zborce that you had just testified to a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because he stated here that the commander of the KLA and their membership did not know each other's names. They referred to each other by nickname. That is why Mr. Fatmir Limaj is here referred to as Celiku. And it says that a meeting was held in the village of Zborce.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Does it say when the meeting was held in Zborce?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: He said it happened three weeks prior because from Zborce the roads lead to the thoroughfare connecting Stimlje and Dulje and there is a road going to the Gornje Godance village, Stimlje municipality, where a substaff of the KLA was later formed led by Enver Mehmeti, also known as Inspector. And that's a man I know personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for just a moment. It says that it happened three weeks prior. Three weeks prior to what date? Sorry, just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to the 28th of July, when the statement was given. The 27th of July, 1998. But this piece of information three weeks prior doesn't necessarily have to be correct. It all depends on how good the memory of the person is, the person giving the statement I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, was this the first time you had heard of a person Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. called Celiku?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I first heard about a person called Celiku in the beginning of July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can we go into private session please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, can you please turn to tab 14 in your booklet. The usher will help you. I'm sorry that it's not a particularly good copy in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This is a statement that I took together with my partner, Mr. Sparavalo, on the 13th of -- on the 13th of August, 1998, on the premises of SUP Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go very briefly into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, if you look at page 2 of this statement I'm going to read out a section if you can just see it and follow along.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can hardly read this myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I know. It's a bad copy. Listen to me for the moment. It says: "The leader of the staff in Petrastica was Ramiz Qeriqi, while his deputy was Latif Musolli. At the beginning of June 1998," it appears to say, "a meeting was held in the Petrastica village primary school and attended by the villagers. The meeting was led by three masked KLA persons who said that Siptar parties no longer existed and that authority was being taken over by the so-called OU." Now, is that a reference to the meeting in Petrastica that you had mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. This meeting was held in the schoolhouse of the school called Idriz Ajeti in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with that document. Now, Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to move away from these meetings to go into a different topic now. And to do that, I would like you to look behind tab 3. This is a criminal report and it says that -- it's dated the 30th of June, 1998. It has a stamp and some signatures at the bottom. Do you recognise those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the stamp of Urosevac SUP and I wrote this report together with my partner, Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go briefly into private session, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'm just going to read to you a couple of passages from this. In the first paragraph it says there: "Around 0130 hours on 27 June 1998 in Gornje Godance village, unknown persons kidnapped Agim, son of Bajram, born on 27 March 1959 from his family house. Also kidnapped was Vesel Ahmeti, son of Isak, from Gornje Godance, born on 2 January 1963; both were taken in an unknown direction." Then further down on the page it says: "According to... statement, that same night, Shyqyri Zimeri, son of Rashit, born on 16 June 1966, in Gornje Godance village was also kidnapped." Now, were those things told to you by the person who made this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. The person from whom we took a statement underlying this criminal report told me this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I draw your attention to the second-to-last second where it says: "The kidnapped persons were loyal citizens of the Republic Serbia." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Before I answer this I would like to come back to some facts. The Albanian terrorists, the so-called KLA, they had a pathological hatred for everything Serbian. And their targets were also all Albanians who did not wish to join the KLA. Albanians who had friends among or socialised with Serbs, Albanians or Siptars who had friends among Serb policemen. And they also targeted Albanians who worked in Serb enterprises or companies and resisted in some way to their violence and terror. What -- this is a reference actually to the citizens of Serbia who lived in conformity with the constitution and the legislation of Serbia. And if you ask me person by person, I can explain to you the motivation behind their kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll come to that later. Let's move on to the next document which is behind tab 8. Actually, this one doesn't need to be on Sanction, Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This is a criminal report dated 8th July 1998. The ERN number for the record is K0225357 to 5359. In the English it's 03056425, 6428. I haven't been very diligent about reading all of the ERN numbers into the record. I don't know if that's absolutely necessary, but if it is I'm come back and clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, just looking at this criminal report, if you look on the last page do you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This criminal report was written by Mr. Sparavalo and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And just looking at the first paragraph. Was Agim Ademi a member of the police reserves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This is a question you had better put to Bogoljub Janicevic, the then-chief of Urosevac SUP. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I guess let me just ask you, at least before the 8th of July, 1998, were you aware of Agim Ademi being a member of the police serve forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I can speak in my own name and on behalf of my partner, Mr. Sparavalo. The two of us were not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This report also references some weapons and some articles of clothing which are described as being given to Agim Ademi by the Urosevac SUP. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I was not aware that the SUP of Urosevac had issued him with anything. If this is true then only the chief or his deputy could know about this. My partner and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. In that case then let's please move to the next document which is behind tab 9. The English is 03048108 to 8111. Mr. Younis can put it on the Sanction for us. First of all, Mr. Jasovic, it says that the source of this is "a friendly contact." Without mentioning the name, who does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: It says the source is a friendly connection or friendly contact from the Albanian national minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember who that person is? If we would go into private session, could you tell me the name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I know who it is but I wouldn't like to mention the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. I don't think it is important, but we can come back to it if it is. Looking at that first paragraph I'm going to read something and I want you to follow along and see if this is an accurate record of what was told to you on that day. It says: "Based on intelligence, Jeta Hasani took part with the rest of the terrorist group in carrying out terrorist operations in Gornje Godance village when on 27 June 1998, Agim Ademi, Vesel Ahmeti and Shyqeri Zumberi were kidnapped and taken away in an unknown direction and their legally possessed firearms were seized from them. He also took part in the terrorist operations at Adem Ramadani's, Shefqet Ramadani's, Eljmi Ramadani's and Ibrahim Smaili, all from Gornje Godance village. Family members of the kidnapped persons recognised Jeta Hasani by his voice during the terrorist operations in Gornje Godance village, but out of fear, they cannot say his name." Mr. Jasovic, is that an accurate record of what was told to you by this source?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see regarding the kidnapping of Zymeri, Ahmeti and Adem Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Ademi, we had information even earlier that the kidnappers were Albanian terrorists, the so-called KLA. Qeriqi Ramiz, Jeta Hasani, and Fehrudin Gashi. With a proviso that Ramiz Qeriqi is from Krajmirovce village, Lipjan municipality; Jeta from Stimlje municipality; and the last one also from Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This operation was easy to carry out because the wives of Fahrudin Gashi and Ramiz Qeriqi were from Gornje Godance, Stimlje municipality, whereas Hasani himself comes from that village. As for my information that my partner and I received, they are accurate. This is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if it's probably time for a break or if I should march on with one more document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, that's a convenient time. Thank you, Mr. Black. We will resume at 5 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just raise one matter very quickly before the examination continues. I'm sorry, I feel right. Quite a lot of the material so far that has been done in private session in fact could be done in public session, particularly where there are named victims who are known on public record and descriptions of what is alleged to have happened to them also in the public domain. So I would ask in fact unless it's absolutely necessary, that we continue in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless I have -- unless I am mistaken, all the discussion of the publicly named victims has been done in public. Where I have gone into private, at least my intention has been just for the names of the people who made the statements and perhaps where they're from or some identifying information about them. But I'm certainly in agreement that besides that a lot of what we can do we can do in public. And I will proceed on that basis, if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to resume my questioning now, and to do that I'd ask you to look behind tab 12 in the binders there in front of you. Perhaps the usher can assist you. We actually looked at this document a few minutes ago. It bears the ERN K0327273 to 7274. And if you could please look at the second page of the B/C/S which is the third page I believe of the English translation. I'm going to read part of it out to you and I would like you to focus on this with a view to whether or not this is an accurate record of what was told to you by this witness. This is, by the way, from a statement dated 28th July, 1998. And it says: "Jeta Hasani from the village of Gornje Godance and Fahredin Gashi from Stimlje, among others, were all involved in the terrorist operations in the village of Gornje Godance, when Agim Ademi, Zmeri Suceri, Ahmeti Veselj and others were kidnapped and taken away. Their involvement was confirmed by" -- I won't read the next part -- "who recognised these two persons when they and some other persons stormed his house in camouflage uniform and carrying automatic rifles." And then if you'll go down to the second-to-last paragraph it says: "As for the persons who were kidnapped in the village of Zborce, Agim Ademi, Zumeri Suceri, and Vesel Ahmeti, I heard that they were in a place called Lapusnik, and that they sometimes took them to a place near Kijevo." Now, Mr. Jasovic, those passages that I've read out, is that an accurate recollection of the information you received from this person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: As for the kidnapping of Agim Ademi, Zymeri Suceri and Veselj Ahmeti and others, apart from this statement we also have other statements. And it's correct they were kidnapped on the 27th of June from their family homes. And in early July 1998 we learned that through Zborce near Mirovac [phoen] and Sedlare they were taken to the prison in Lapusnik. The kidnapping was carried out by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fahrudin Gashi from Stimlje, municipality of Stimlje, and Jeta Hasani from Gornje Godance municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, let me interrupt you for just a second and it's just really to ask you to speak a little more slowly because I notice the interpreters sometimes are having trouble catching the names. Can you just repeat the names you said of the people who carried out these kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The kidnappers of these persons were: Ramiz Qeriqi, known as Duan [as interpreted], from the village Krajmirovce, Lipjan municipality; Fahrudin Gashi, known as Faki, from Stimlje, municipality of Stimlje; Jeta Hasani from Gornje Godance, municipality of Stimlje; and there were a few other unidentified Siptar terrorists of the so-called KLA who took part in the kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. I'm not sure if there was a mistake perhaps in the transcript. What is -- what was Ramiz Qeriqi known as? What was his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Zuan [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you spell that, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Luan, L-j-u-a-n [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I think that's clear. Sir, you mentioned that in early July 1998 you learned that these people were taken to the prison in Lapusnik. How did you learn that information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I learned it from a registered operative connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is this the same registered informant that we named earlier in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I think we can move on to the next document. This one is behind tab 14. This is a statement dated 13th August, 1998, and we looked at a part of it earlier. But if you could turn to page 3 in the B/C/S or page 6 in the English version. I'm just going to read out a couple of passages and again focus on them to see if they are an accurate record of what this witness told you. That's what I'm interested in for the time being. It says: "At the end of June, beginning of July, a terrorist group from Petrastica village was operating in Gornje Godance village and had kidnapped the following persons and taken them in an unknown direction: Agim Ademi, Vesel Ahmeti, Shyqeri Zimberi and Adem Ramadani." And then a bit further down from that, I think it's the next paragraph, says: "The terrorists, Jete Hasani and his group, took the kidnapped persons, Agim Ademi, Vesel Ahmeti, Shyqeri Zymberi and Ademi Ramadani, to a prison in Klecka." Is that an accurate record of what this person told you on the 13th of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: All the kidnapped persons of Serb or Albanian ethnicity, regardless of whether they were kidnapped on the premises of the village of Crnoljevo or Gornje Godance, both in the municipality of Stimlje, according to our information were not taken directly to the prison in Lapusnik. But the persons, because this part of the road from Gornje Godance leads through the village of Zborce, Krajmirovce, Klecka, Sedlare, to Lapusnik. And probably these persons were taken to the first KLA staff first and then to the prison in Lapusnik. I assume that this is correct and that first they were taken to Klecka and -- to Klecka and then to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At the time this statement was taken on the 13th of August, 1998, had you already received information that these people had been taken to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, we learned this from a registered informant.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And why didn't you -- why didn't you include this information in this statement? Why didn't you say in there that these people had been taken to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: There are notes and there is information. We had to leave the area, I mean the secretariat of the interior, in a day. So these were left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I think -- it may be too obvious a question or too simple, but if you knew or you had heard that these people had been taken to Lapusnik, why didn't you put is that in this statement here of the 13th of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I -- if I might. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that the question is objectionable on a number of grounds not the least being that this statement as I understand is attributed to a specific individual as opposed to being an official note or any other form of memorialisation of this particular witness. Also, I believe that the answer is clear because of the rest of the information that is contained in that which Mr. Black was just reading which is after the word to a prison in Klecka, it says "Once there, they were tortured and then thrown into a well. I don't know what happened to them." Perhaps that might answer Mr. Black's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether that was an objection or an offer of assistance, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I deal with that first?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. This is a statement from a witness and if this is apparently what the witness said, you could confirm that. But to go on and ask why this witness didn't add to what a witness was telling him in a statement information that he had at another time from another source, this is something quite unhelpful and objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I certainly agree with that. And I think the purpose of my question was so subtle it might not be noticed. I wasn't asking him to say why another witness didn't say this. I was not focused on the substance. I was focused on the procedure of taking a statement and I was asking him why he didn't put things that he knew into the statement. But I'm happy to move on. I wasn't trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We seem all to be assuming that a statement would reflect what the person making the statement said. That may not be a valid assumption in this world, but I think that's what we can expect people here to work on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Very well, and, Your Honour, I believe the witness testified to that exact manner earlier. Generally speaking, I thought this might be an example. But I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, is there something more?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour has done it for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right. We'll just leave it at that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. Jasovic, if you'll turn to the next document which is behind tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, the ERN of this documents is 0188-6157 to 6158, and it's a statement dated the 8th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, would you look at this document and see if you can find your name and signature on the last page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature and that of Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo, Srboljub Vojinovic, and Miroslav Antic, and there is a seal of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you take this statement, you and these other gentlemen or these other individuals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these other three took the statement together with me, the other three signatories I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go briefly into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if you could just look, Mr. Jasovic, at the first page of this statement. It's on the second page of the English translation which Mr. Younis has put on the Sanction. It says there, and please follow along: "While Fahredin Gashi was staying at my house, I asked him who had kidnapped Agim Ademi, Shyqyri Zymberi, Ahmeti Veseli from Gornje Godance village." And there's a blank there, it says "replied that he had taken part in the kidnappings of these persons together with KLA commander Ramiz Qeriqi, Jete Hasani, and others, whose names he didn't mention. He explained how they had used Lada Niva vans, taken the road in Gornje Godance that goes by the Zborce River and then returned the same way once the operation was finished. He said that they had taken Agim, Vesel and Shyqyri to the 'KLA' staff in Krajmirovac, from where they were taken to a location near Kosovska Mitrovica where they were tortured in a well, and then transferred to an unknown location." Mr. Jasovic, was that information given to you by the person who made this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct because I know this person. I knew that person long before, 15 or 20 years before. And he himself came to the premises of the Urosevac police station to tell me about this. It's a fact that Fahrudin Gashi's father, Haradin Gashi, brought Fahrudin's wife to the village of Gornje Godance, Stimlje municipality, and Fahrudin Gashi as a KLA member used to come with Mr. Luan and Jete Hasani to visit his wife. In my view this correction is correct. Zete Surak [phoen] conducted the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever receive other information about these three men being taken to a location near Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this information, we as a service and I personally did not receive any other information. It's possible they took them to Kosovska Mitrovica in order to physically maltreat and torture them because all information indicates that the three kidnapped persons were subjected to violence and torture by Albanians belonging to the so-called KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to the next document which is behind tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The ERN number of this document for the record is U001-0689 to 0690. It purports to be a statement of September 9, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, do you see your name on the last page of that document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I see my name and that the statement was taken by Momcilo Sparavalo, an inspector of the public security, and Darko Amanovic, an inspector of the state security of the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And were you present when this statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and besides me these two persons were also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go briefly into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I'd like you to look with me, Mr. Jasovic, at the first paragraph of that statement where it says: "Your office is well aware of the incident that took place at the end of June this year when Siptar terrorists from the KLA came to Gornje Godance village, Stimlje municipality, and kidnapped... Agim Ademi, whose fate remains unknown. Subsequently, we heard from the villagers in Gornje Godance that Agim had been kidnapped by the following: The 'KLA' commander for Petrastica and Krajmirovac, whose nickname is Luan; by Jete Hasani, from Gornje Godance; by Fahredin Gashi, from Stimlje, and others whose name I don't know. This had all been ordered by Jete Hasani." And then the next sentence which says: "He also knew where Ahmeti Veseli and Shyqyri Zymberi, another two persons that were kidnapped, resided." Now, Mr. Jasovic, was this information given to you by the person we just mentioned in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. We received this information from the person I mentioned previously. And I would like to point out that when Agim Ademi was kidnapped by the Siptar terrorists, the commander Ovak Haceric [phoen] and Ramiz, Luan, they threatened the family of the victims in case they reported the case to the police station in Stimlje or to our secretariat in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can move to the next document; it's behind tab 23. The ERN number is 0188-6164, a statement dated 10 December 1998. Mr. Jasovic, do you see your name, signature, and a stamp there at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see my name and authorised officials Momcilo Sparavalo and Darko Amanovic -- Jasovic [as interpreted], and also the seal of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you and those other men take this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The three of us took this statement and throughout the taking of the statement we were all present.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go briefly into private session, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you look at the first paragraph of this statement. It says: "I live in Gornje Godance village, Stimlje municipality, and I heard from the villagers there that at the end of June 1998 'KLA' members forcefully took the following persons from their homes and took them in an unknown direction: Shyqyri Zymberi, Ahmeti Veseli and Agim Ademi. Their fate remains unknown to this day. I heard that these persons were kidnapped by Ramiz Qeriqi, aka Luan; Fahredin Gashi, aka Faruk; and Jete Hasani, who were KLA members in the Petrastica and Krajmirovac village areas." Mr. Jasovic, was that information given to you by the person that we -- that gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We received this information from the person who gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm -- I'll ask you to turn to the next document behind tab 24. For the record the ERN of this document is 0188-6166. It's a statement dated 14 January, 1999. Mr. Jasovic, do you see your name or signature on the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was taken by me, Momcilo Sparavalo, and Srboljub Vojinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go briefly into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, again I'll ask you for you to follow along with me. I'm just going to read a couple of parts of the first paragraph. It says: "I know that in June 1998 Agim Ademi, Shyqyri Zymberi, and Vesel Ahmeti were kidnapped from their homes after 2300 hours and taken in an unknown direction by the following members of the so-called 'KLA': Ramiz Qeriqi, aka Luan; Fahredin Gashi, aka Faruk; and Jete Hasani and his group. These KLA members kidnapped Ademi Ramadani and Shefqet Ramadani from their family homes and took them to Gornje Godance village. They were released 25 days later and allowed to go home." Mr. Jasovic, the same question that I've been asking before: Was this information given to you by the person that made this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The person who signed the statement gave this information on the 14th of January, 1999. It was clear to everyone who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with that document. Now Mr. Jasovic, did you know any of the men that we have been discussing personally? I mean Agim Ademi, Vesel Ahmeti, Shyqyri Zymeri, Adem Ramadani or Shefqet Ramadani. Did you know any of them personally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I knew all three of them. Shyqyri Zymeri was a person I knew and probably the motive for his kidnapping was that a patrol of a police station when patrolling Gornje Godance would stop at his shop, Zymeri Shyqyri's shop, and would probably have a drink there. The Siptar terrorists of the so-called KLA didn't like this because they thought he was giving interesting information, of interest for our service, to the policemen who entered his shop; this was not correct. Vesel Ahmeti I think was a member of the SPS and a member of the temporary Executive Board formed in Kosovo and Metohija and that was the reason for his kidnapping. As for Agim Ademi, he associated with all good people, regardless of their ethnic affiliation. He didn't care whether someone was a Serb, an Albanian, a Turk, or belonged to some other ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know if any of those men, Shyqyri Zymeri, Vesel Ahmeti, or Agim Ademi were paid informants of the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not true that they were paid informants of the police, that is of the secretariat of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Ademi Ramadani and Shefqet Ramadani. Did you know either one of those men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Shefqet Ramadani because he was an electrician and I know he was kidnapped and taken to the prison in Lapusnik and that he was released I think on the 25th of July, 1998. As for Adem Ramadani, I knew him by sight. I would sit in a catering establishment with Shefqet. I'm referring to Shefqet Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: As far as you know, were either of those men Adem Ramadani or Shefqet Ramadani paid informants of the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Neither was. Neither was an informant of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. Now I'm going to move on to a somewhat different topic, a different group of victims. If you turn back to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. beginning of your binder, please, to the document behind tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, this document bears the ERN 0188-5946 to 5967. It's a statement dated 29 June, 1998, it's behind tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, do you see your name and signature and a stamp on the second page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this statement was taken by my partner, Momcilo Sparavalo and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who gave this statement? And you can say this name in public session.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This statement was given by Mrs. Vesna Bakrac on the 29th of June, 1998, on the premises of the secretariat of the interior, Urosevac. In Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what was the subject of this statement? What did Mrs. Bakrac tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: On the said day around 1100 hours, the police -- the policemen of the police station in Stimlje informed the chief of the Urosevac SUP that an incident had happened on the main road from Stimlje via Crnoljevo to Prizren whereupon the chief of the secretariat Bogoljub Janicevic summoned me and told me, Dragan, go to Stimlje. Because some Serbs had been kidnapped in Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me focus on -- specifically on what Mrs. Bakrac told you. Did she say -- did she tell you what happened to her or to the people with her?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived at Stimlje, when we arrived at the place where the police checkpoint was, a location overlooking Stimlje facing Crnoljevo, there was a bus standing there, the driver standing outside. And he told us the story. When we arrived, there was this woman, Vesna Bakrac, lying on the ground crying. And she was saying, Please get me back my husband and son. We barely managed to calm her down and we took her into her car and drove her to the police station in Urosevac. We had told the bus driver to follow us to the secretariat. On the spot and later he told us that several Siptar terrorists, members of the so-called KLA --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, Mr. Jasovic, I'm sorry, maybe I haven't put them in the best order. I'm going to show you a couple of documents. But please for the moment let's focus on the statement of Vesna Bakrac on the 29th of June, 1998, and tell me, did he tell you what happened to the people that she was with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: She told me that Siptar terrorists had stopped the bus on the main road. This was a regular service from Djakovica towards Pristina, stopping in Crnoljevo and Stimlje. She said that these KLA members got into the bus and asked the driver, Are there any Serbs in here? They demanded that everybody show them their IDs and they took out Mr. Bakrac, the father, and Ivan Bakrac, the son of the woman, along with two other Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You said that the bus had been stopped on the main road. Which main road? Could you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This road goes from Prizren, Suva Reka, Stimlje, to Pristina, and they were stopped in the centre of the Crnoljevo village on the main road. So this all happened in the centre of Crnoljevo village, Stimlje municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did Mrs. Bakrac have a chance to review and sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: She reviewed the statement and signed it. We took her to Pristina and she cried all the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would move this document be admitted into evidence. I haven't done that with the others because I've just been trying to focus on the important bits, but this document -- in fact the entire thing refers to this incident. I would ask that it be given the next exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 4 would be given Prosecution Exhibit Number P205.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could move then, Mr. Jasovic, to the document behind tab a 5. For the record, the ERN is 0188-5967. Mr. Jasovic, this is another statement from the 29th of June, 1998. Did you take this statement as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, together with Mr. Sparavalo. It was taken on the premises of the secretariat of the interior of Urosevac in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And who made this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was given on the 29th of June, 1998, by Nexhat Kosturi. I don't know whether it was the driver or the person checking the tickets on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If it would refresh your memory, you can refer to this document to tell whether it was the driver or the conductor.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: It's the conductor, actually. The conductor who worked on the bus with Djakovica licence plates. I see it's Shpetim Skivjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need to read this out, but I would ask you to take a moment and read this to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, does this statement relate to the same incident that you were just discussing with us about Vesna Bakrac's statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It refers to the persons who were kidnapped, Vojko Bakrac, Ivan Bakrac, and two other persons. At the time, we thought it was a Serb victim but we identified him later as Genov, Stamen. I don't know what ethnicity is that. And another victim was named Cuk. He was either from Bosnia or Croatia, I can't remember which.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Does this statement here in front of you, does that say where the people were kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement matches the information given by Mrs. Vesna Bakrac. They were kidnapped from the bus in the centre of Crnoljevo village, Stimlje municipality while following the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Does it give any description of the perpetrators, the kidnappers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Here below it says: "I demanded" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I asked the man to describe the perpetrators."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this receive the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 5 would be Prosecution Exhibit P206.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move to the next document which is behind tab 6. For the record the ERN is 0188-5950 and it is another statement dated 29 June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you take this statement, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: It was taken by me and Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was given by Mr. Shpetim Skivjani, occupation bus driver. Bus with Djakovica licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Does this relate to the same incident that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
