utterances.text: Yes. It relates to the incident in which the bus with the Djakovica licence plates was intercepted on the main road in the centre of Crnoljevo village and four persons were taken off the bus and kidnapped, Vojko and Ivan Bakrac and two other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did this person give a description of the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did, in the second half of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that it receive the next exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 6 would be Prosecution Exhibit P207.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'll ask you now to look at the next document behind tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, the ERN is 0188-5938 to 5939 and it is a criminal report dated 30 June 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you prepare this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This criminal report was written by me and Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo based on the statements we had taken from the driver, from the conductor, and from Vesna Bakrac. This criminal report was filed relating to the criminal offence of terrorism, Article 2 of the Criminal Code, and it was forwarded to the competent public prosecutor's office, district prosecutor's office in Pristina because the municipal court did not exist. There was only the district court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. In addition to the statements, did -- were you able to gather any physical evidence regarding this incident? And by that I mean any documents or other items besides witness statements.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: After reporting an incident, the usual procedure is that the SUP of Urosevac continue to work on shedding more light on the events, and in the course of the investigation we established that the Siptar terrorists cut off the main road, Dulje and his partner set up a checkpoint there, stopped all traffic, demanded IDs from all passengers. When they stopped a bus they would inquire if there were any Serbs among the passengers and they would also target Albanians whom they considered disloyal or dishonest and they would take them off the bus and away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I think my question wasn't very clear. What I meant was: On the 29th of June, 1998, in addition to talking to Mrs. Bakrac and the driver and the conductor, were any items found?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. On the bus itself we found some clues that helped us identify Mr. Genov, Stamen, one of the victims. We found a chequebook and some other documents he had left behind. I can't remember the details. Mr. Genov, Stamen, was an active-duty army officer. I believe his little bag was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If it would refresh your recollection, maybe you would like to look at this criminal report and see if that reminds you which items were found.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: A pistol of the Crna Zastava type was found, 45-millimetre calibre, serial number 294913, 15 cheques of the postal savings bank with the number of his savings account: 11471714, on which occasion we also established his identity. He was Genov, Stamen. We also found his travel bag and some other personal items, including money in the amount of 150 German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jasovic, who recovered those items, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember who recovered those items, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if it was my colleague, Mr. Sparavalo, or maybe Mr. Rado Radovic, another employee of the Urosevac SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't know if you've already mentioned the name, but were you ever able to determine the identity of the fourth person taken from the bus in addition to Vojko Bakrac, Ivan Bakrac, and Stamen Genov?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as this fourth person is concerned, we managed to establish his identity only a year ago. Mr. Branko Debeljkovic, head of the criminal investigation police was in charge of the case. This department covers general crimes and white-collar crimes. This is the department I work in myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what identity were you able to establish?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: We established that it was a Mr. Djordje Cuk, a refugee, who lived as a refugee in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And do you remember how you were able to establish that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This is how it was: His brother, whose name I don't remember, reported the case to the International Red Cross in Belgrade and some other international agencies, also in Belgrade. This brother said that his brother had set off on a trip by bus with Djakovica licence plates. He cited the date and the time of departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, before it escapes me, could I ask for the next exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab number 7 would be Prosecution Exhibit P208.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, after the day of the kidnappings, did you have any further contact with Vesna Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: We talked to her almost every day because she had left for Pristina and she found a place to stay there and reported the case to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ICRC. She called us every day to ask if we had found out anything new about her husband and her son, and every time she would call I would ask her if she had received any new information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you learn anything about the fate of her husband and her son?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, we found on the 6th of July, 1998, that Mr. Vojko Bakrac and his son Ivan had been released. We found this out from some policemen. Vojko and Ivan had come back from the direction of Crnoljevo, and in Stimlje they were stopped by the police from the MUP of Serbia. On this occasion I, with the approval of my superior, the chief of Urosevac SUP, Mr. Bogoljub Janicevic, went out to talk to Vojko and Ivan Bakrac, but I was not given access to them by the ICRC. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted). There is an official note relating to this and there is also the letter that we sent to the competent authorities of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Just one small point of clarification. You said that Vojko and Ivan Bakrac were stopped by the MUP in Stimlje. Were they alone when they were stopped or were they with someone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: They were not alone. There was a driver with them and some other people. I can't remember unless you let me read this document, this letter. But it's certain that they were not alone. They were accompanied by people from the ICRC, who were escorting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Were you ever able to learn in your investigations what happened to them between the day they were kidnapped and the day they were released?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Everything we learned about Albanians and Serbs who were kidnapped, specifically in the Stimlje municipality in Crnoljevo village, in Belince village, Petrovo village, Gornje Godance, all of these villages belonging to Stimlje municipality, indicates that they were taken via Petrastica, Krajmirovce, Sedlare, Kvocka, towards Lapusnik prison, or from Gornje Godance through various villages ending with Klecka to the Lapusnik prison in Glogovac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to ask you to look at another document now. It's behind tab 10 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, the ERN is 0188-8642 to 8643. It's a statement dated 21 July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you take this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was taken by me and my colleague, Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, please follow along with me. In the first paragraph of the statement it says: "I can't remember the exact date but I know it was sometime at the end of June 1998 when I personally saw Rrahman Tafa and Ramadan Lushi, both from Crnoljevo, stopping vehicles from the Stimlje-Crnoljevo-Dulje main road, near the old school. They were checking identification documents, searching passengers in the vehicles." And then a bit further down it says that a person "told me that Rrahman Tafa, Ramadan Lushi and another person, whose name I don't know, had come to a store and when the three of them left they had stopped a bus that was travelling in the direction of Stimlje. While checking identification documents in the bus, they had removed four Serbs and took them in the direction of Drenica - to Lausa village I think - through Petrastica and Krajmirovce. After a while I heard that two of these people had been released." It continues: "As far as Rrahman Tafa and Ramadan Lushi are concerned, I heard that the two of them in their group had come down to Petrastica village on the main road and had stopped vehicles on the stretch from the centre of Crnoljevo to the old school in Crnoljevo. Their intent was to kidnap Serbs and those Siptars who were loyal citizens." Mr. Jasovic, was that information given to you by the person we had just mentioned in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. This information was obtained from the person we mentioned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: There are a couple of references to Ramadan Lushi. Do you know if that person was ever known by another name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Ramadan Lushi is in fact Ramadan Behluli. They call them Lushi by their grandfather or great-grandfather.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before I move away from that document, a little further down it says: "Two or three weeks ago I saw Rrahman Tafa, Ramadan Lushi and Naim Azemi... all from Crnoljevo, in a white Lada Niva vehicle on the Crnoljevo-Petrastica dirt road." Then I'll skip a sentence. And then it says: "The owners of this white-coloured Lada Niva are brothers Vehbi and Fehmi Tafa, whose last name is also Tafa, but their father is Xhem. I know this Lada stays in Petrastica village and is used by terrorists to travel to places where terrorists operations will be undertaken." Mr. Jasovic, was this information also given to you by the person who gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was the the person who gave the information. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll ask you o move to the next document; it's behind tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The ERN of this document for the record is 0188-5956. It's a receipt dated 1st of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I handed over documents to a military officer carrying out military security tasks. On the 1st of August, 1998, I returned to this person items belonging to sergeant Stamen Genov: One pistol, Crna Zastava, 7.65 millimetres in calibre; one ammunition clip with a 7.65-millimetre shells; 150 German marks, serial number -- I don't know if I need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You don't need to read the serial numbers and I'll ask you to go slower. But in fact you don't need to read that all out. Can you just tell me where these items were all found.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The items were found in the bus with a Djakovica licence plate in front of the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac where the bus was parked. In order to interview the driver and the conductor of the bus bearing a Djakovica licence plate as well as with Vesna Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And just so it's 100 per cent clear, is this the same bus that we had discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The bus that was stopped on the 27th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this receive the next exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab number --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stopped in Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab number 13 would be Prosecution Exhibit P209.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to ask you to turn to the document behind tab 14 again. We've looked at it before. I'm going to ask you about a different part. This is the statement dated 13 August 1998, with ERN U000-1414 to 1417. Mr. Jasovic, you should look at page 3 of the B/C/S version and it's page 6, the top of page 7 in the English. Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to read out another part to you and I want you to listen and see if this is the information you received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For your information, Your Honours, the Sanction doesn't seem to be working very well, so we're not going to get this document up on Sanction. But I'll proceed anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, if you can follow along. It says: "I also know that the terrorist operations on the Stimlje-Dulje main road were carried out by so-called KLA terrorists: Skender Hasani (son of Shefli) from Petrastica; Ramadan Behluli (son of Muharrem) from Crnoljevo; Rrahman Tafa from Crnoljevo; Ali Gashi (son of Ramadan) from Petrastica; and Jete Hasani from Gornje Godance. On one occasion they stopped a bus at a cafe in the centre of Crnoljevo with automatic weapons, removed four Serbs and took them to Klecka." Mr. Jasovic, does that refer to the same incident that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it refers to the bus with the Djakovica licence plate which was stopped on the 29th [Realtime transcript read in error: "27th"] of June, 1998, on the main road in the centre of the village of Crnoljevo municipality of Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember the -- you mentioned the 27th of June. Do you remember the date that the bus was stopped?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The bus was stopped on the 29th of June 1998 after 11.00 during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I just noticed an error in the transcript and I wanted to clarify that. The sentence in that document, Mr. Jasovic, if you could look again where I was reading before. It says: "Subsequently these same persons stopped a black Golf 3 vehicle and threw its Serb driver into the trunk and took him to Krajmirovac in his own vehicle. I do not know where they took him after that." Was this information also given by the person who gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: This information was given by the person who made the statement. The secretariat of the interior in Urosevac did not identify the kidnapped person. It's possible that the person was identified by officials from the Prizren secretariat of the interior. This is probably a person from Prizren because he was travelling from Prizren towards Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm done with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you receive other information about Serbs being kidnapped in your area during June and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Our service, the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac received information that in that area on the main road in the village of Crnoljevo, Stimlje municipality, the following persons were kidnapped: Srboljub Miladinovic, who I know personally. He was a traffic policeman working in Stimlje, and his employment was terminated, I don't know for what reason. Then Miodrag Krstic, known as Mijo, and his brother or relative. The persons were from Suva Reka municipality. And Zivorad Krstic born in the village of Musnikovo, Prizren municipality, residing in Pristina. And from the same bus another Serb was kidnapped whom we were unable to identify. We have information that all the persons who were kidnapped were taken to the prison in Lapusnik in Glogovac municipality. Near Velika Stena is where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that an appropriate time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. We will resume at 5 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am sorry that it was necessary to have a longer break than planned because of the need for a redaction which only came to my attention after we had adjourned. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'm going to continue my questioning and to do that I would like to ask you to look at the documents behind tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, the ERN in the B/C/S version is K022-5715 and the English is 03058555 to 8557. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you take this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I, Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo, and Mr. Srboljub Vojinovic took this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we go into private session briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, you can just please have a look at this document with me. I guess I'll read out the section I want you to focus on. It says: "When we arrived above the village of Petrovo, before the entrance in the Ljuzak mahala, two KLA members in a red Lada Niva caught up with us, made us show our identity cards, and ordered us to turn back. I did not know these people, but I later learned that one of them is nicknamed Dula [sic] and is originally from Drenica while the other one is nicknamed Cak and his first name is Isak, but I do not know where he is from. I got into the Lada Niva, which was driven by Cak, while Dula got into the TAM with Izrija. They took us to the so-called KLA's headquarters in Rance, at which point Cak threw me out of the Lada Niva and kicked me and punched me several times and then Dula and Cak drove off Hizrija in a blue Lada Niva to Drenica. I later learned that they took him to a prison in a place called Lapusnik and to this day I do not know what happened to him." Sir, was this information given to you by the person we just identified in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The person I mentioned on the 6th of October, 1998, gave this statement because Hyzri Hajrizi from village Belince, municipality of Stimlje is his uncle and in June of 1998 driving a small TAM truck he went to buy some lime from a lime from a certain Qamil Uka. As the

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: vehicle set out towards the village of Petrovo, Stimlje municipality to buy some sugar and vinegar. At the first checkpoint at the exit of the village of Rance he was stopped by two brothers Azem and Agri Huzijo [phoen] and they let them go on in the direction of the village of Petrovo. However, at the entrance to Luzjak mahala, which is about 2 kilometres from the village of Petrovo in the direction of the village of Rance, in this vehicle two persons arrived with pseudonyms Cak and Dull and later on I learned from the list of the KLA what the details of these persons were, of Cak and Dull that is. Ramadan Azemi entered the vehicle of the person nicknamed Cak while Dull got into the TAM. They were sent back and returned to the KLA headquarters in Rance in Stimlje municipality. In the village of Rance in the KLA headquarters, they were interviewed and after that, according to our information Dull and Cak took Hyzri Hajrizi to Lapusnik prison in

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: of the headquarters and beaten up and then he was told to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I think you said you learned the details of Cak and Dull. Who were those people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Cak was Isak Thaqi and Dull is Abdulla Rama. If you will allow me to look at the list I can tell you where they are from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Would looking at the list help you refresh your recollection? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have the list I think he was referring to. It wasn't on the exhibit list because I was -- the possible exhibit list because I was not intending to tender it. Perhaps I could show it to Defence counsel and he could have a look at it. I think it may refresh his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's something that has not been seen by the Defence yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It has been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could this be passed first to Defence counsel and then to the witness. And perhaps, Your Honour, while that's being looked at I think we -- it would be good to have a redaction page 65, line 9. There is a name mentioned. If we could have that redacted, please. I believe it was mentioned twice, once at the beginning of a paragraph and then a couple lines down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Younis informs me that page 64, line 19, is the other mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is that the list you had asked for, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is one page missing from the beginning I believe. Under number 1 there is a person named Isak, last name [sic] Cak, born on the 18th of June, 1968, in Komorane, Glogovac village, nicknamed Caki. Number 4, first name Abdulla, last name Rama, born 17th July, 1968, in Sankovc village, pseudonym Dull. But there is a cover page missing where commander Qerqiz or Qerqiz is mentioned. I have it in my bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I don't think we need to get that out, but just to be clear, your testimony is that these are the details of Cak and Dull which were mentioned in the statement that we were looking at early. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, because from some statements obtained by ethnic Albanians -- obtained from ethnic Albanians, there is a reference to Ismet [as interpreted] Thaqi, local of Komorane. And there is the mention of this 121st Brigade, Rance Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In fact, if I could ask the usher to take that document back and give it back to Mr. Younis. For the record, perhaps I should read -- the ERN of that document is U004-7727.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I would like to ask you to look at another document now. It's behind tab 20 in your binder -- actually, Mr. Jasovic before you get there, I'm sorry to interrupt you. My colleague raises a good point. On the transcript it says -- when we were talking about -- when you were looking at this document that I'm holding up, U004-7727, the transcript says: "There's a person named Isak, last name Cak, nicknamed Thaqi [sic]." Is that the correct name of this person that we were talking about? I'm focused on the surname.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: It's Isak, last name Thaqi, pseudonym Cak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sorry for that interruption. Now I'll turn you to the document behind tab 20 which I think you have open before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, the ERN of this document is U000-4585 to 4586, and in English it's 0303-2855 to 2860. I apologise, Your Honour, I have a discrepancy in my numbers. Mr. Younis, hopefully, is about to save me. I'm sorry, the B/C/S ERN number I gave was wrong; it's in fact K022-5711 to 5714. The English number was correct. Thank you, Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, could you please have a look at that document. Did you take this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I took it together with my colleague, Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we please go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, if you could look at page 2 of the B/C/S statement. It's page 3 of the English version. Please follow along with me. I just want to read one paragraph to you. It says: "Two months ago, KLA members kidnapped... Hyzri Hajrizi, son of Oruq, from the village of Belince, Stimlje municipality, who was on his way to get whitewash. I went to the KLA staff in the village of Rance three or four times to inquire... and find out where they had taken him, and when I asked to see the commander, Zimer Kurtisi came to see me and angrily told me that he was the commander's deputy and asked me what I wanted, before ordering Dula to talk to me. Dula told me all of us SPS, short for Socialist Party of Serbia, members and spies ought to be killed, and slapped me a few times across the face. Dula also told me he and a man with a nickname of Cak had taken Hyzri to prison in the village of Lapusnik." Sir, did you receive that information from the person that we just identified in private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I got this information from the person whose name I mentioned just a minute ago, and this person, as I said, is the nephew of the kidnapped person who went to the KLA headquarters to inquire about

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted). And eventually Dull talked to him and said, naturally, you SPS members will eventually all be killed. And after that, this person was beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Jasovic, I appreciate the information, but it's not necessary to repeat all the things that I read generally speaking about. Could you turn to the next page, please, which is a supplemental statement. This is on page 5 of the English translation. Just follow along. I'll read out this short paragraph at the very beginning of the supplemental statement. It says -- do you find it, Mr. Jasovic? It says: "I would like to supplement my previous statement by saying that... Hajrizi Hyzri, from the village of Belince, Stimlje municipality, was kidnapped and taken away by the members of the so-called KLA on the orders of brothers Afrim and Agnija Musliju, sons of Isljam, who told members of the so-called KLA that Hizrija socialised with the Serbs and the Serbian police." Mr. Jasovic, did you receive this information from the same person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was the date of this supplementary statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st of October, 1998, it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you take that supplementary statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with my colleague, Srboljub Vojinovic and Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. I'm going to ask you to look at another document now. This one is behind tab 15 of your binder. It's a statement dated 8th September, 1998, and we looked at it briefly earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you take this -- actually, I think we covered that ground. Let me just focus your attention on --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we went through this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me focus your attention on the last page, the second-to-last paragraph, and I'll just read out the last two sentences. It says: "In Gornji Lapusnik, I was taken by 'KLA' members and brought to the staff and after five or six hours of questioning, I was released. They had inquired about Safet Hisenaj from Petrovo village and asked what he did and who he kept company with." Sir, did you receive that information from the person who signed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the person who signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you know Safet Hyseni personally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I had known him about ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him because he liked to socialise with police inspectors in Urosevac and we first met in Stimlje. When inspectors would sit down in a coffee bar, he would approach and sit down with us. And it was a state security agent Srboljub Vojinovic who introduced us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Safet Hyseni a police informant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, earlier -- I'm going to go back to some names that we talked about because I forgot to ask you a question. I asked you about Agim Ademi and Vesel Ahmeti and Shyqyri Zymeri and whether they were paid informants and you said they weren't. Were any of these men informants, police informants of any kind, paid or unpaid?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: You mean all three of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, any one of them or all three of them.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: None of them was an informant of the police or the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about the Shefqet Ramadani, was he a police informant of any kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not. It's just that he liked to have a drink with inspectors, police, when they would come to a coffee bar and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about the Ademi Ramadani, was he a police informant of any kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasovic. I'm going to ask you to look at another document. This one is behind tab 19. For the record, the B/C/S ERN is K022-5692 to 5693. The English is 0306-5483 to 5484. Mr. Jasovic, did you take this statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I did, together with Momcilo Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we briefly go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, if I can focus your attention on the second-to-last paragraph, I'm going to read you a couple of sentences. Please follow along. It says: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, should I -- I'm afraid we're going to have to redact that. Should I go back and go over it again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I apologise. I'm going to have to read that out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Hasan, can you take that off the screen please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It says: "I can also state that Muj Musliju from the village of Belince" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's a good way to handle it. If we could go into private session, Your Honour, this way I can read it without.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I gather you're about to move on to a fresh topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
